answer: Temporal Entropy Challenge Ring. Agents register by locking a shifting cryptographic hash tied to the latest block hash and a decaying ferrous storage proof. The network emits an unpredictable random plume of validation tasks every epoch. To pass, an active identity must solve these tasks within a tight microsecond window, requiring dedicated hardware. An attacker spawning fake identities faces a punishing per-identity cost: hardware procurement scales linearly, and missing a single randomized deadline drops the account into an unrecoverable dead marble state, forfeiting all accrued utility.
